item.title: What I've learned after my first month of coding with Rust
item.description:
In my previous article I talked about my very debut in the coding world and why Rust is my choice (I just love Rust).

The most important lesson

Since I finished RareCode , for about a week I struggled a lot. I was wondering: “What’s next?”.

I’ve tried to:

  • read a book (Learn Rust in a Month of Lunches ) that I’ve already talked about, and it was really valuable until the chapter covered a topic that I haven’t previously understood and practiced.
  • follow tutorials, but it was really short because I just don’t like that.
  • start a personal project with Leptos , well… my skills need some improvements before Leptos. I didn’t understand a lot of things while going through the documentation.

My attempt to create a personal project was maybe a little bit too rushed. But because of that I’ve found Codewars , did a lot of kata (all the 8 kyu in Rust) and progressed a lot.

item.title: Why I'm Learning Rust as My First Programming Language
item.description:
It took me around 8 months of procrastination, but at one point I finally finished 739 Rust exercises, as a non-programmer.

Let me tell you the story of a non-programmer (yet) learning Rust as his first language.

JavaScript, SaaS and illusions

At the very beginning, I was wondering what to do in my life, what I really wanted to do in my life I mean. I watched on YouTube a video about AI and SaaS… I won’t go deep here, you can picture the story. Just some random beautiful thing that makes money, but the reality is different.
